# Dr. Christine L. Clark

Dr. Christine Clark is a native of Maryland; growing up she spent summers enjoying Lewes and Rehoboth Beach.

She joined the hospital as a veterinary assistant in 1990 and after graduating from Ross University School of Veterinary Medicine in 1996, she returned to Lewes, Delaware. Dr Clark became a partner of Savannah Animal Hospital in 2014.

Her veterinary interest include internal medicine, ultrasonography and chemotherapy.

Dr. Clark lives with her husband, Tony, daughter, Emma, and three dogs, Brew, Benjamin and Marnie. As a family, they are always planning and looking forward to their next Caribbean adventure.

Margaret Musser, DVM, DACVIM (Oncology)
Dr. Margaret Musser is our Board Certified Oncologist. She was born and raised in Delaware, Ohio. She received her B.A.
cum laude in Biology from Colby College in Waterville, Maine, with minors in Chemistry and Theater. After her
undergraduate studies, she worked as an oncology veterinary assistant at MedVet in Worthington, Ohio. In 2010 she
graduated with honors from the College of Veterinary Medicine at the University of Illinois. Dr. Musser then completed a
one-year rotating internship in small animal veterinary medicine at VCA West Los Angeles before beginning her residency
in medical oncology at North Carolina State University's College of Veterinary Medicine. Upon finishing her residency in
2014, she joined the team at VCA Veterinary Referral and Emergency Center in Norwalk. In her spare time, Dr. Musser
enjoys running, yoga and sailing.

## Dr. Allison Gedney, DVM, DACVIM (Oncology)

Oncology

Dr. Allison Gedney is our newest medical oncologist. She is a Delaware native and attended the University of Delaware for her undergraduate degree in Pre-Veterinary Medicine while ru nning competitively for UD for 3 seasons all 3 years.  Dr. Gedney started her veterinary schooling at Ross Universi ty in St. Kitts, but transferred to Oklahoma State University after her first year to get more involved in the world of oncology. During her time at Oklahoma State, she assisted in a laboratory researching temperature sensitive nano-particles for chemotherapy delivery. After completing her Doctorat e in Veterinary Medicine in 2016, she returned to Delaware, completing her rotating internship at the former Veterinary Specialty Center of Delaware.  During this year she met current PETS Doc tors, Walsh, Goldkamp and Knox. After her rotating internship she became a member of the University of Pennsylvania Comprehensive Oncol ogy Team as their intern, managing radiation, medical and clinical trials oncologic cases.

  * # ​​Veterinary Acupuncture

  * Image

Humans have been using acupuncture as a medical treatment for thousands of years and its benefits have been making waves in veterinary medicine. Our staff has additional specialized training in this unique treatment modality and we are eager to see if it is right for your pet!

Pain-free Treatment
One of the most important aspects of any of the services that we bring to your cat or dog is ensuring that they get the treatments they need in a painless or minimally traumatic manner as possible. The insertion of acupuncture needles is done in a specific manner in precise locations to ensure that there is no pain and to give your pets a sense of comfort throughout the entire experience in order to maximize its benefits.
 
Pain Management
There are two main focuses when it comes to providing pet acupuncture: pain management and pain relief. If your pet is post-operative any procedure, undergoing chemotherapy for cancer treatments, or has another chronic condition causing them discomfort, choosing to look into acupuncture can provide them with the pain management solutions you’re looking for. We are dedicated to bringing a comfortable and enjoyable experience to your pet and giving them the best quality of life they can have.
 
Musculoskeletal Issues
Whether your dog is suffering from arthritis or your cat from a traumatic injury earlier in life, acupuncture can be a great way of reducing the pain through proper blood flow and instigation of white blood cell production. Acupuncture cannot only make it easier for your pets to get through their day but also allow them to focus less on the pain that’s being experienced and more on the experiences they have with you.

At Haven Lake Animal Hospital, we understand that you may feel a bit overwhelmed by it all, but rest assured that we are here to help and guide you and your pet through the process and back to health.
More and more tests are moving from the larger laboratories to the clinic setting. As a hospital, this gives us the answers that we need quickly and allows us to not delay in developing the best plan for the pet. Forget the old hand held x rays. Digital radiographs are quick and easy to share. Need to see a specialist? We can take those survey films here (at a lower cost to our client) and send them directly to the specialist or for a professional review. How about an ultrasound guided aspirate of that suspicious mass? We just happen to have an ultrasound here for our patient’s convenience. No need to travel one or two hours away for these diagnostic tools because great service is what we aim to provide. Orthopedic surgery? Chemotherapy? Joint injections? We can help you with that.

### Referral is a Service Too

Specialized medical care, particularly when it involves advanced diagnostics, complex surgeries, critical care, and highly trained board-certified veterinarians, inherently comes with higher costs than routine general practice veterinary services.
  * Internal Medicine: Diagnosis and treatment of complex internal diseases affecting various body systems, such as endocrine, gastrointestinal, cardiovascular, respiratory, and kidney issues, often involving advanced diagnostics like endoscopy and ultrasound.
  * Surgery: Performing a wide array of advanced surgical procedures, including orthopedic (bone and joint), soft tissue, and emergency surgeries, often utilizing advanced anesthetic monitoring and pain management.
  * Cardiology: Specializing in the diagnosis and treatment of heart and lung conditions, including congestive heart failure, arrhythmias, and congenital defects, often involving echocardiography and electrocardiography.
  * Diagnostic Imaging: Utilizing state-of-the-art imaging tools such as MRI, CT scans, and advanced ultrasound to provide detailed views for accurate diagnoses.
  * Oncology: Comprehensive cancer diagnosis, staging, and treatment, which may include chemotherapy, radiation therapy, and surgical oncology.
  * Neurology/Neurosurgery: Addressing conditions of the brain, spinal cord, and nervous system, including seizures, paralysis, and spinal injuries.

**32.8 CRITERIA FOR WHEELCHAIR SERVICES**

Services other than car, minivan or public transportation may be required when one of the following conditions is present:

a. The member requires a wheelchair and is unable to use public transportation;  
b. The member has a disabling physical condition which requires the use of a walker, cane, crutches or brace and is unable to use a car, minivan, commercial taxi or public transportation;
